default.like: One of the reasons I like using Slack is that everything related to communication and discussion of a project is in one place. It enables me to exchange messages, post questions, share files, and discuss other things without switching between various programs. I also appreciate the use of channels, which allow staying more organized in case there are several projects at hand and several people involved.
default.dislike: It is often challenging for me to keep up with critical updates when there are several communication channels open at once. There are a lot of updates and sometimes I need to go back and search for a specific one. I believe that there is some room for improvement in the area of notifications management, especially when working on several tasks at once.

default.like: What I like best is how clean channels and threads keep team discussions, different projects don't turn into one giant messy group chat. Also huddles are super handy when you just need a quick 2-minute voice call or screen share to debug something with a teammate without setting up a whole calendar invite.
default.dislike: The notification overload can get pretty overwhelming once you're in a few active channel, important updates get buried fast, and it's easy to lose track of older context. Also, the 90-day message history limit on the free tier is really annoying if you need to look back at old discussions or links, and the desktop app eats up way more RAM than a chat tool should.

default.like: What I like best about Slack is its easy-to-use interface and ability to make team communication quick and efficient. It helps me stay connected with colleagues, share updates, ask questions, resolve work-related queries, and collaborate on tasks in real time. I also like the channel-based communication, file sharing, and quick notifications, which make it easier to manage multiple projects and stay updated on important discussions.
default.dislike: What I dislike about Slack is that managing multiple channels and conversations can sometimes become overwhelming. Important messages or updates can easily get buried in busy channels, and frequent notifications can interrupt work. Searching for older discussions or specific information could also be more intuitive. Better notification management and improved message organization would make the overall experience more efficient.

default.like: What I like most about Slack is how it keeps team communication organized without having to rely on long email threads. I use separate channels for development updates, project discussions, bug reports, and general team communication, which makes it easy to find the right conversation later. Threads are especially helpful because replies stay tied to the original message instead of cluttering up the main channel. I also appreciate being able to share files, screenshots, code snippets, and links directly with teammates in the same place. Integrations with tools like GitHub and Jira make it easier to keep up with development updates without constantly switching between different applications.
default.dislike: The volume of notifications can get distracting, especially when several project channels are active at the same time. At times, important messages end up buried under everyday conversations, and tracking down older discussions can take a bit of effort. I also find that managing multiple channels and keeping notifications under control takes some initial setup and adjustment.

default.like: What I like most about Slack is how easy it makes it to be part of a technical community. I've used an open-source community's workspace, and it is great having discussions, questions, updates, and knowledge shared by people in the same field and in the same org all in one place. I can follow conversations that are relevant to me, learn from what others are working on, and participate whenever I have something to contribute. The channels and threads are some of the features I really like, as they make it easier to keep track of discussions without getting lost in one big chat.
default.dislike: Honestly, I don't have many major complaints. If I had to pick something, it would be that Slack can feel a little overwhelming in very active communities. With so many ongoing discussions and notifications, it's easy to miss something interesting or lose track of conversations you want to revisit. I would also like to have a bit better search experience when it comes to bringing up old discussions when looking for a specific topic.
